text_summary: During welding operations on the P-2291 permit boundary, a portable multi-gas detector positioned near V-204B showed H2S spiking to 18 ppm. The area gas sensor GD-204 read only 6 ppm due to calibration drift identified during the subsequent investigation. A field supervisor halted welding and increased ventilation; if GD-204 had been the sole monitor, the rising gas concentration would not have triggered an evacuation alarm until well above the 10 ppm STEL.

Compressor C-12 ran for approximately 90 minutes with lube oil level below the minimum mark after a sight-glass fitting developed a slow weep. The high-vibration alarm had been placed in suppressed mode during a prior balancing exercise and was never restored. An operations technician discovered the low oil condition during a routine field check; the bearing temperature was trending 15°C above normal but had not yet reached the trip setpoint.

A routine turnaround inspection of heat exchanger HX-503 found that the channel-end gasket had developed micro-cracks consistent with repeated thermal cycling between 40°C and 260°C. No leak had occurred in service, but the gasket material had lost 30% of its rated bolt-load retention. The gasket was from a batch that had already been flagged for accelerated replacement across the site.

Two simultaneous work permits were active on V-101A — a vessel-entry permit for internal inspection and a line-break permit on the downstream piping. The portable LEL monitor inside the vessel showed 3% LEL while the external fixed detector read 0% due to a zeroing error during morning calibration. An HSE coordinator reviewing the permit board identified the overlap and halted both activities until a single coordinated isolation plan was established.

During a splash-loading transfer of toluene into storage tank T-402, a visible static arc was observed between the fill pipe and the tank shell. Investigation found that the bonding jumper cable between the road tanker and the fill manifold had corroded terminations giving a resistance of 450 ohms instead of the required <10 ohms. The transfer was halted and a replacement bonding cable installed. No ignition occurred due to the tank's inerted atmosphere.

Flare stack FL-401 pilot flame extinguished during a period of sustained 65 km/h crosswinds when the pilot gas supply pressure dropped below the minimum 0.5 barg due to a partially closed block valve on the pilot gas header. The flameless condition lasted approximately 7 minutes before the thermocouple low-temperature alarm alerted the control room operator, who dispatched a field technician to manually reignite the pilots. During the outage, no process gas was being routed to the flare.
